'''Team Event Format''' is [[Decipher]]'s team scoring for Star Wars CCG tournaments: teams of three or four players enter a normal sanctioned event, and each team's three best finishing places are added together. Decipher ran team events at conventions in 1999 and closed each season with a team event at DecipherCon.<ref name="teamrules99">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/teamevents/rules.html Star Wars CCG Tournament Team Events: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000109210353/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/teamevents/rules.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="team99">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/teamevents/index.html Star Wars CCG Tournament Team Events], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990901032216/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/teamevents/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' team scoring on a constructed or sealed-deck event
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (1999)
* '''Card pool:''' that of the host event
* '''In use:''' 1999 – 2000
* '''Also called:''' Team Swiss scoring; DecipherCon Team Challenge (DecipherCon 1999 and 2000);<ref name="dc99-sun">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sun_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule (Sunday)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026063736/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sun_events.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="dcon-sw-events">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game events], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010126213800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Internet Archive].</ref> DecipherCon Constructed Team Event (DecipherCon 2000 schedule)<ref name="dcon00-sched">[http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf DecipherCon Master Tournament Schedule for Decipher Games], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030413152501/http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Rules ==
Decipher's 1999 rules:<ref name="teamrules99" />
* "The beauty of the Team Event format is that it seamlessly blends with normal Constructed or Sealed Deck protocols." Players not on a team may play in the same tournament.
* Teams have 3 or 4 players. A captain picks players from his area (city, town or school). A registered player must play at least 2 tournaments with a team before switching.
* At least two teams must register with the director before play for team scoring to apply. The tournament itself is run as normal.
* After the event the director adds the three highest finishing places of each team; a fourth player's place does not count. The lowest total wins.
* Ties are broken first by head-to-head record between the two teams' players, then by total team differential; if still tied, it is a true tie.

== History ==
In 1999 Decipher listed team events at Origins 99, GenCon Game Fair 99, Euro GenCon Antwerp, San Diego ComiCon, Spiel 99 Essen and DecipherCon 99, each "offering a large 4-piece trophy for the winning team". Teams registered on Decipher's website.<ref name="team99" /> "Decipher will end this year's season of Team Events by holding the crowning Team event tournament at DecipherCon 99."<ref name="teamrules99" /> DecipherCon 1999 scheduled the Star Wars DecipherCon Team Challenge (SW.06) on Sunday 14 November 1999, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; results are on [[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]].<ref name="dc99-sun" />

At [[DecipherCon 2000]] the DecipherCon Team Challenge (#SW141, Sunday 8 October 2000, 10 a.m., four games, sanctioned) "follows the same format as Decipher's team events of the summer conventions with one major addition - wherever possible, no player will be paired against a player on their own team!" Teams had 3 or 4 players, and decklists were required.<ref name="dcon-sw-events" />

Decipher's DecipherCon 2002 formats page described a "Team Tournament" for ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG and ''Star Trek'' CCG in the same terms: teams of three or four, never paired with a team member, top three results per team count.<ref name="dc02-formats">[http://www1.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventformats.html Event Formats], DecipherCon 2002, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021017051130/http://www1.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventformats.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The Players Committee's Alternate Format Tournament Guide has a different team format: two-player teams, one playing Dark Side and one Light Side, with the match decided by the two games.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>
